title: Resting-home wiring unpinned: boot/run-reset/deselect/ESC call sites have no driving test — reverting any to camera_set_fit passes the entire suite
evidence: app/main.odin:972 (start_run): `// eases, across a run boundary) + no class focus + no stale selection diff.` / `camera_set_default(app)`. app/main.odin:1133-1136 (effect_cancel): `effect_cancel :: proc(user: rawptr, ictx: ^inp.Input) {` / `	app := cast(^App)user` / `	camera_set_default(app)` / `}`. app/main.odin:1800 (camera_set_selection deselect tail): `camera_set_default(app)` / `}`. app/pullback_test.odin:393-394: `	camera_set_default(&app6)` / `	testing.expect(t, !app6.pullback, "ESC home yields the pullback")` — the test labeled 'ESC home' calls camera_set_default directly, never effect_cancel. harness/goldens.odin:23-24: `// Render_Ctx — the harness's render setup: the palette + camera-fit view +` — goldens never run the app camera. Verified: no test drives effect_cancel, the selection-diff deselect leg (main.odin:697), or start_run; reverting all three call sites to camera_set_fit keeps core 261 / render 81 / app 43 / harness 49 demos / palcheck green (all run at sha 9bf9797).
detail: The feature's headline behavior (resting home on entry/reset/deselect/ESC) is pinned only at the callee. All three call sites are mutation-invisible; goldens capture at camera-fit and never exercise app camera wiring.
recommended_fix: Add app-package tests driving the real entry points — effect_cancel via input.on_cancel, the selection-diff deselect, start_run — asserting cam targets == DEFAULT_ZOOM / home anchor.

title: PUCK_GROWTH_MAX cap has no effective coverage: shipped tier ratios (1.14/1.27) sit below 1.30, so deleting the min() clamp fails no test
evidence: app/render/sprites.odin:274: `return 1.05 * v.tile_px * v.scale * min(sh.bboxes[idx][2] / base, PUCK_GROWTH_MAX)`; sprites.odin:255: `PUCK_GROWTH_MAX :: 1.30`. assets/sprites/sprites.json widths: puck_1 `[62, 106, 132, 121]` (base=132), puck_2 `[53, 98, 150, 137]` (150/132=1.136), puck_3 `[44, 90, 168, 153]` (168/132=1.273) — both under the 1.30 cap, so the min() is a no-op on every shipped sprite. Repo grep: sprite_puck_target is referenced only by call sites (view.odin:1627-1628, wire_path.odin:126), never by a test.
detail: The 'future-proof ceiling' guard is vacuous today: removing min() or raising the cap changes zero pixels (ratios < cap) and no unit test exists — the project's mutation-leg blocker shape (font r5 gate-10 precedent).
recommended_fix: Unit-pin sprite_puck_target with a synthetic Sprite_Sheet (bbox ratio > 1.30 clamps to exactly 1.30) plus tier ordering: puck_1 < puck_2 < puck_3 targets.

title: Sub-default pullback band (zoom in (1.0, DEFAULT_ZOOM]) is a designed silent no-op but has zero pins
evidence: app/render/camera.odin:221: `z_to = clamp(min(z_x, z_y), DEFAULT_ZOOM, CAM_ZOOM_MAX)`; camera.odin:226-228: `if z_to >= zoom {` / `		return zoom, center_x, center_y, false // the clamp already covers it` / `}` — for zoom < 2.0 with an out-of-view district, needed < zoom < 2.0 so z_to floors to 2.0 >= zoom: active=false, never fires (old code eased out to 1.x). The design is only a comment — app/pullback_test.odin:302-304: `// pinned: the pullback settles at the cluster default, never the` / `// whole-map fit (a camera already AT 2.0 with a distant seed is a no-op` / `// by design — the floor equals the current zoom — the accepted tradeoff)` — and the test was moved to 3.0 instead of pinning the no-op at 2.0.
detail: Behavior changed in the reachable manual-wheel-out band (the spec's out tier): a distant seed now silently does nothing below the default. A >=/> flip or floor tweak regresses without any test failing.
recommended_fix: Pin camera_pullback_target at zoom=1.5 and zoom=2.0 with a far out-of-view district → active=false, targets unchanged; note the band in the doc comment.

title: Dublin block growth (B) pinned only via pixel goldens — no unit pin of the block-vs-puck legibility ratio the directive actually names
evidence: app/render/dublin.odin:67-68: `DUBLIN_NODE_BLOCK_L :: 0.55 // long axis (along the street)` / `DUBLIN_NODE_BLOCK_W :: 0.30 // short axis`. Repo grep: DUBLIN_NODE_BLOCK_* referenced only at dublin.odin:348-349 (draw math) — no test file references them; coverage is the re-blessed T2 goldens only (mutation-guarded: any constant change shifts node frames red).
detail: Absolute sizes are pixel-pinned (mutation-guarded), but the relative property — 'a high-tier puck stays just above a terminal block instead of ~3x it', the user's complaint — is asserted nowhere.
recommended_fix: Add a cheap unit pin comparing block footprint (L x W x tile_px) against sprite_puck_target ordering so the legibility ratio cannot silently re-invert.

title: PR body claims palcheck floors were re-pinned; the diff contains no palcheck change and the commit says 'no re-pin needed'
evidence: _pr_body_camera_zoom_tiers.md:58-60: `- **palcheck floors re-pinned where the puck shrink dropped pixel counts**` / `  (e.g. the puck hardware-tone floor) — measured on the re-blessed frames,` / `  keeping the crop/blit-canary job (a missing sprite still zeroes the count).` But `git show HEAD --name-only` lists exactly: _pr_body_camera_zoom_tiers.md, app/main.odin, app/pullback_test.odin, app/render/camera.odin, app/render/camera_test.odin, app/render/dublin.odin, app/render/sprites.odin + 113 goldens — harness/palcheck.odin unchanged; the commit message itself reads `palcheck stays green (floors had margin) - no re-pin needed`. I ran the harness palcheck leg at the sha: `palcheck: all green`.
detail: The declared spec's re-bless section misdescribes the test suite. No functional hole — palcheck floors held with margin (verified green) — but the PR body contradicts the commit.
recommended_fix: Correct the PR body's re-bless section to the commit's account: floors had margin, palcheck green without re-pin; drop the 're-pinned' wording.
